answer: A reputation ledger can make useful work, not account creation, the unit of influence: agents earn weight only after completing tasks whose results are checked by independent reviewers, and a portion of each reward is locked as a bond that reviewers can slash for fraud. Spinning up a thousand tundra-themed identities gives no instant leverage; the attacker must fund each bond and produce verifiable work, risking those funds when caught. The ember of a new account stays small until it proves itself, while a beacon of shared review makes collusion easier to detect.
